items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary: Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] “Robots are advancing quickly, but developing them for real-world environments remains slow, data-intensive and difficult to scale,” Huang said. “Working with UC Berkeley, NVIDIA is helping advance a new approach combining agentic AI, simulation and open industrial task-focused benchmarks to help developers rapidly test and improve robot behavior before deployment.” [...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger.

items.title: Top Robotics Stocks With Strong Potential for Long-Term Growth
items.summary: With orders accelerating, humanoid pilots becoming contracts, surgical robotics gaining regulatory clarity and defense autonomy topping budget priorities, U.S. robotics enters 2027 with diversified demand drivers, positioning sector leaders well as adoption scales across factories, hospitals and homes. [...] U.S. robotics stocks enter the final stretch of 2026 on firmer footing, as September through early November brought a wave of commercial deployments, regulatory progress and government funding signals. North American robot orders hit their strongest quarter of the year, humanoids moved from demos toward contracted factory work, the FDA outlined a clearer path for surgical robots, and the Pentagon made autonomy a top budget priority. Together, these developments point to a broadening demand base [...] U.S. robotics demand strengthened through the fall. The Association for Advancing Automation reported that North American companies ordered 10,989 robots worth $723.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 24.8% year over year, with semiconductor and electronics orders nearly doubling. Humanoids moved closer to factory floors as Boston Dynamics opened its Robotics Metaplant Application Center in Georgia on Sept. 21 to train Atlas for Hyundai, which plans to deploy 25,000 units globally.

items.title: Inside App State’s Robotics Lab: Students explore the future of human–robot collaboration | Appalachian Today
items.summary:
Students work with a variety of robotic platforms, including robotic arms that handle objects, humanoid robots such as Pepper and NAO that are designed to interact with people and mobile robots that can move through an environment while manipulating objects. These platforms help students explore how robot behavior, movement and communication influence interactions with people. [...] Current lab projects focus on helping robots better understand and respond to the people around them. Researchers are investigating how robots can adapt their behavior over time, work safely alongside people and use different types of information to make more informed decisions.

One research area examines how robots can adjust their actions as people move nearby, an important challenge in workplaces where humans and robots share the same space. [...] This brief video offers a behind-the-scenes look at the Yeganeh Robotics (YeRo) Lab in App State’s College of Arts and Sciences. Demonstrations include a Go2 quadruped robot, often called a “robot dog,” navigating its surroundings while maintaining balance, and a robotic arm transferring an object between locations on a workbench. These examples illustrate the types of robotic systems and research questions student researchers are exploring in the lab.

items.title: Agility Robotics' Nasdaq debut invites scrutiny of humanoid robot market - Ars Technica
items.summary: Humanoid robots remain unproven at scale and have not yet achieved widespread commercialization, compared with industrial robots that have decades of proven track records in warehouses and factories. That frank acknowledgment is among the risks outlined in a securities filing by Agility Robotics—the first dedicated developer of humanoid robots to become a publicly traded company in the United States. [...] Beyond the challenges of building its own business, Agility’s financial disclosures also cautioned that “competition in the humanoid and robotics market is intensifying rapidly, with well-funded entrants including Boston Dynamics, Tesla, Apptronik, Figure AI, 1X Technologies, Sanctuary AI, Hexagon, and NEURA Robotics, among others, actively developing competing humanoid systems.” [...] In exchange for renting or purchasing the robots, customers would get access to the latest Agility robot known as Digit 5 starting in 2027. The bipedal robot has swappable end-effector “hands,” can lift up to 50-pound loads, and can perform more than 20 hours of work in a 24-hour period with the help of a fast-charging battery system.

items.title: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots | TechCrunch
items.summary:
Serve Robotics already makes two kinds of robots, the cute googly-eyed sidewalk delivery robot and one designed for hospitals that it got through its acquisition of Diligent Robotics.

Those businesses are not going away, Kashani emphasized in a recent interview. Instead, he said there is opportunity to sell the technology it developed for its own robots to other companies developing robots for farms, warehouses, and other uncontrolled environments. [...] Specifically, Serve Robotics will offer customers its connectivity and data tools. Bedrock Robotics, a startup developing self-driving systems for construction equipment, is a customer, according to Serve. It’s also working with T-Mobile to bring AI computing power closer to robots, Serve announced alongside its third-quarter earnings on Thursday.

“We are solving the problem of robots in human spaces,” Serve Robotics CEO and co-founder Ai Kashani told TechCrunch. [...] Serve Robotics, a maker of self-driving sidewalk delivery robots, is expanding beyond its autonomous delivery operations in a bid to become a technology supplier to other companies building robots.

The company, which spun out of Uber’s acquisition of Postmates in 2021 and went public in 2024, said Thursday it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services.

sktime, qwen3, deepeval and timescaledb.

→ qwen3: the large language model series from alibaba cloud's qwen team

how they fit:

1. sktime is the eyes: the close landed inside its 90% band on 27 of 30 days
